reviewer_role: Independent of the author. Personally read all 206 complete actual Job 18-26 sources, full narrative and speaker context, all 136 original complete source-target-category-rationale triples in my own immutable snapshot, and all 21 final corrected complete triples. The final 135 retained rows comprise 114 unchanged rows already read and 21 corrected rows read separately; the grammatical-continuation-only row was removed. Personally read all 71 final complete source deferrals and reasons and all five complete candidate triples with necessary context. My first case snapshot already included the author’s four corrected source reasons and three corrected candidate rationales; it is byte-identical to the frozen final case bundle. Also read all historical changed case wording and reconstructed both exact case stages. Independently fetched and verified 23 own fresh raw bodies and HTTP headers. This independent peer adds no completion credit.

deferred_source_units.reason: The respondent heading identifies Bildad but supplies no separate substantive relationship beyond the speech comparisons.
The least people hunting belongings and the wish that his counsel stumble are preserved without assigning particular hunters or an episode of confiscation.
The actual thirsty person made strong against the victim is not replaced with a robber to manufacture a familiar trap parallel.
The pains around the person and severe famine near his feet do not establish a distinct named siege, famine or judgment episode.
The extraordinary fall prepared for him remains Bildad's prediction; no separately supported event or personal identity is established.
Death devouring beautiful things and the branches of feet is not rewritten as the firstborn of death or identified with an angel of destruction.
The healing, dwelling, distress and royal-charge wording does not name a king of terrors; no personified death-ruler identity is retained.
The wish to thrust him from light into darkness is too unspecific to identify a distinct expulsion or eschatological event.
The unrecognized person and unpreserved house are not rewritten as an explicit assertion that he has no offspring or descendants.
The last people's groaning and first people's astonishment do not specify named generations or observers whose identities can be resolved.
The Job response heading locates the speaker but is not counted as a separate substantive comparison.

Job's admission of error is grammatically qualified by the actual continuation at 19:4a. That necessary contextual reading is preserved, but merely linking the two pieces of the sentence earns no independent connection credit; it is not a confession to the friends' later social accusations.
Job's claim that the Lord disturbed him and raised a stronghold against him supplies no identifiable historical siege or named stronghold.
The removal of glory and crown is preserved; the considered psalm wording says consecrated thing rather than crown and is not used to claim an exact crown correspondence.
Job's trials and encircling men lying in wait are not identified with a particular invading army or the prologue's raiders.
Household neighbors and maidservants treating Job as foreign do not establish a named exile or ethnic identity beyond his complaint of alienation.
The unanswered call to Job's servant describes this household relationship without identifying the servant with another narrative figure.
The supplied appeal to his wife and sons of concubines is retained without importing offensive breath or identifying those sons with the children killed in chapter 1.
Job's disowning and the speech against him whenever he rises provide no separately established target beyond the surrounding abandonment account.
The everlasting one who will release Job upon earth is not explicitly identified by name; the separate Christ-mediator candidate remains unresolved and receives no credit.
Job speaks of what he knows with himself and his eye has seen; this is not changed into the familiar future assertion that he will see God.
The heading identifying Zophar the Minaean establishes the disputant but is not retained as an additional name-only connection.
The spirit answering from understanding is Zophar's reported source of reply; it is not independently identified as the Holy Spirit or a prophetic commission.
The lesser men destroying sons and the pains of hands are not changed into a statement about sons repaying poor people.
Holding evil in the throat continues the eating metaphor; no separate comparison beyond the retained sweetness-to-poison relationship is established for this unit.
The absence of remaining food and failure of good to flourish do not identify a particular famine or provide an independently distinct wealth connection.
The iron hand and bronze bow do not establish a named weapon, battle, archer or historical flight.
The unkindled fire and harm by a stranger do not identify the fire's physical origin or a specific stranger; no such identity is supplied.
The house dragged to destruction on a day of wrath is not assigned to the prologue's house collapse or to a specific final judgment event.
The response heading marks Job's turn and earns no separate connection credit.
Job asks to be lifted up so he may speak and says the hearers will not laugh; the line is not rewritten as permission to mock him afterward.
Job's question about human reproof and anger remains part of his response without being generalized into a separate law or judgment scene.
The required hand is upon the cheek, not over the mouth; no silence parallel is retained by importing a different bodily gesture.
Remembering the ordeal agitates Job and takes hold of his flesh; no distinct illness, vision or episode is identified from that bodily reaction alone.
The cows' successful reproduction is a concrete detail of the prosperity argument, without an established identity with a particular herd or fertility promise.
The enduring sheep and playing children do not establish a distinct flock or child group beyond the surrounding account of prosperity.
Seeing one's own slaughter and failing to obtain deliverance remain part of Job's recompense discussion without a named execution or victim.
The question about care for a house after one's months are divided supplies no separate historical inheritance dispute or verified target.
Abundant inner fat and marrow complete the prosperous person's description; the unit is not counted separately merely for repeating the comparison retained at 21:23.
Job identifies insolent pressure from his hearers, but this conversational accusation alone does not establish a separate particular target.
The wording relieved for a day of destruction and led away for a day of wrath leaves the relation to that day uncertain; the separately read judgment candidate is unretained.
The question who will declare the wicked person's way or repay him does not identify a particular judge, accuser or later judgment episode.
The transport to tombs and vigil over a coffin are preserved without assigning this burial to another named person's funeral.
The source says stream pebbles are sweet to him, not sods of a valley; that distinct image is not normalized to create a burial parallel.
The heading identifies Eliphaz's reply but is not counted as a separate substantive relationship.
The question about reproof out of consideration is not replaced with the familiar because-of-your-fear wording or treated as God's own verdict.
The charge of partiality and settling certain people in the land does not identify a particular land grant or establish that Job actually committed it.
The cloud concealment and circuit of heaven belong to Eliphaz's attribution; they do not independently prove Job held the quoted view or identify a distinct divine journey.
The ancient unjust path remains unnamed; it is not assigned to a specific antediluvian generation without further evidence.
The early seizure and river over the foundations do not name Noah or the flood; the separate Genesis candidate is an unresolved event identification.
The obliteration of substance and fire consuming the remainder are not assigned to a specific city, household fire or destruction event.
The mound, rock and torrents of Ophir do not explicitly name gold in this unit; the Sophira gold-voyage candidate does not establish the same material or episode.
The actual restoration of a dwelling of righteousness and bright ways is not rewritten as a promise that whatever Job decrees will occur.
The response heading identifies Job but contributes no separate substantive connection.
The first-things and end wording is preserved without replacing it with east and west or importing a complete compass-direction parallel.
Agitation and concern follow Job's description of divine freedom; no distinct particular comparison is established beyond the retained fear-and-hearing tension at 23:15a.
The Lord softening Job's heart and the Almighty agitating him are not normalized into a technical hardening or faintheartedness formula.
The donkeys, field activity and sweet bread for young ones have uncertain human referents; no caravan, wilderness tribe or named foraging group is identified.
The wet people clasping a rock for lack of shelter remain Job's concrete picture without identifying a specific cave refuge or storm narrative.
The actual ambush in narrow places and ignorance of the righteous road are not replaced with oil pressing or wine treading from another version.
The failure to recognize the earth and righteous roads is not changed into an explicit rebellion-against-light phrase to force a verbal parallel.
The switch between He who knows and hands people to darkness and he like a thief does not securely identify the thief; no day-of-the-Lord comparison is retained.
Lightness upon the water's surface and a cursed earthly portion do not establish a particular drowning or named person's fate.
The second woman is not explicitly called a widow in this unit; its barren-woman and mercy language is preserved without importing that identifying term.
The wish that the weakened person not hope for recovery and the prediction that he will fall by disease are not rewritten as God granting him security or ease.
The respondent heading supplies Bildad's name but no additional substantive connection.
The actual prelude, fear and phrase makes the whole in the highest are preserved rather than replaced by a familiar declaration of dominion and heavenly peace.
The supplied reprieve for raiders and divine ambush are not rewritten as a count of armies or light shining on everyone.
The heading marks Job's response and carries no separate supported connection.
The question about whose breath the hearer speaks does not establish prophetic inspiration or identify that breath as the Holy Spirit.
The giants brought to birth beneath water are not replaced by trembling shades; their identity with Genesis's giants remains unresolved in the separate candidate.
